title: Jaki-ed fine mat
summary: In the Marshall Islands the finest mats are plaited from pale, hair-thin pandanus strands, with dark strands drawing bands, diamonds and a bordered edge. Copy the pattern, which mirrors left to right.
howToPlay: Pick a strand colour and a pattern shape.
Place it; the mirror partner is plaited too.
Check the mat against the pattern.
Watch and learn shows a finished round, one placement at a time.
rules: The mat mirrors left to right.
Placing the same shape in the same colour again, or choosing the eraser, clears it and its mirror partners.
The result compares your piece with the pattern cell by cell: three stars at 98 percent or more, two at 85, one at 60.
The pattern to copy is always shown beside the work and as a faint guide on the cloth.
heritageNote: Jaki-ed are the finest mats of the Marshall Islands, plaited from very thin, pale pandanus strands by makers who keep the skill within their families. They are given and kept as valued gifts.
credits: Pattern designs are original arrangements in the tradition's motif vocabulary.
